findings.title: Fix-task detection checks only the branch tip commit subject
findings.desc: The harvest decides "is this a fix task" via `git log -1 --format=%s "$TIP_SHA"`, but the new prompt has agents run a multi-step pre-ship sequence (review-fix iterations, retro doc) before committing, so the tip commit can easily be a `docs:`/`test:`/non-conventional subject — and conventional-commit prefix is only "preferred," not enforced. Any such task's retro is silently excluded from harvesting; scanning all branch commits (e.g. `git log --format=%s main..$TIP_SHA`) for a `fix:`/`fix(` prefix would be far more robust.

findings.title: Harvest skip paths are completely silent
findings.desc: Empty `BRANCH_TIP_SHAS[$TASK_ID]`, non-matching subject, missing retro, or an empty `FIX_RETROS` all skip with no log line, so an operator cannot distinguish "no fix patterns this round" from broken wiring (e.g., `BRANCH_TIP_SHAS` never populated — it is not visible anywhere in the provided material). A single echo/log entry when the harvest finds nothing would make the feature's failure mode observable.

findings.title: Fix-task detection keys off only the branch tip commit subject
findings.desc: The harvest decides "fix task" by matching `fix:`/`fix(` against the tip SHA's subject alone, but agents commit freely and the final commit (made after the retro, per the new prompt) may carry another prefix (`docs:`, `test:`) or the fix may be a non-tip commit. Such tasks are silently skipped, so their `Failure pattern:` notes never reach the library — fail-open with no warning logged.

findings.title: `BRANCH_TIP_SHAS` population is unverifiable from the provided material
findings.desc: The harvest loop reads `${BRANCH_TIP_SHAS[$TASK_ID]:-}` but no assignment to this array appears in the diff or the committed context; if it is unset, or holds pre-implementation (base) SHAs rather than post-agent tips, every lookup yields an empty/wrong subject and the entire Step 5b harvest silently no-ops. Confirm it is populated with post-implementation tip SHAs for approved tasks before this point.

findings.title: Fix-task detection misses eligible retros
findings.desc: Harvesting examines only the branch tip subject and accepts only lowercase conventional `fix:`/`fix(...)` prefixes, while the implementation prompt merely prefers conventional commits and permits multiple commits. A task containing a shipped fix but ending with a retro/docs commit—or using a descriptive non-conventional subject—will silently lose its failure pattern.

findings.title: LLM changes are committed without enforcing append-only behavior
findings.desc: The harvester instructs Claude not to modify existing entries, but then commits any diff to the library without checking that changes are append-only or schema-conformant. A malformed run can rewrite or delete accumulated failure patterns despite the documented append-only invariant.

findings.title: Empty failure-pattern library can abort under pipefail
findings.desc: If the library has no `FP-[0-9]+` entries, `grep` returns nonzero; with `pipefail`/`errexit`, the assignment can terminate the script before `${NEXT_FP:-0}` supplies its intended fallback.

findings.title: “Every task” review guarantee is false
findings.desc: The consequence claims every task clears a multi-critic review, but gate 1h explicitly skips when `claude` is unavailable or its output is unparseable. The document should describe this as best-effort or state those exceptions.

findings.title: Failed harvests can commit partial or invalid edits
findings.desc: The `claude` exit status is discarded with `|| true`, after which any detected change to `failure-patterns.md` is committed without checking schema compliance or that existing entries were untouched. A failed or interrupted invocation that partially edits the file can therefore corrupt the append-only library directly on the merged branch.

findings.title: Fix detection only examines the branch tip
findings.desc: Harvesting considers only the final commit subject, so an approved multi-commit task containing an earlier `fix:` commit is skipped when its tip is a review, test, documentation, or retro commit. This conflicts with the stated rule that shipped fix commits contribute failure patterns and silently loses the intended cross-round learning.

FINDINGS:
1. scripts/self-improvement.sh:~1444-1452 | Medium | correctness | `git log` not scoped to repo | The new Step 5b calls `git log -1 --format=%s "$TIP_SHA"` without `-C "$REPO_DIR"` (or a `cd`), unlike the `FP_LIB`/`RETRO` paths right next to it which are built from `$REPO_DIR`. If the loop's cwd at this point is a worktree or temp dir rather than the main repo, this silently fails (`|| echo ""`) and the task is treated as non-fix, quietly breaking the whole harvest for that task.

2. scripts/self-improvement.sh:~955-975 (prompt) vs ~1444-1451 (harvest filter) | Medium | consistency | Harvest depends on undocumented `fix:` commit-prefix requirement | The harvest step only pulls `Failure pattern:` notes from tasks whose final commit subject matches `fix:*`/`fix(*`, but the implement prompt only says "conventional-commit prefix preferred" and never tells the agent that using `fix:`/`fix(...)` specifically is required for its failure-pattern note to be harvested. An agent that fixes a bug but commits as `chore:`/`refactor:`/`fix!:` (bang breaking-change form, also unmatched by the case pattern) will have its documented failure pattern silently dropped with no warning.

3. scripts/self-improvement.sh:~1438-1443 | Low | correctness | Unverified dependency on `BRANCH_TIP_SHAS` | Step 5b indexes an associative array `BRANCH_TIP_SHAS[$TASK_ID]` that is not defined anywhere in this diff (nor visible in the inlined context); if it isn't populated elsewhere in the (not-inlined) script, `TIP_SHA` is always empty and the loop `continue`s for every task, making the entire failure-pattern harvest a silent no-op. Worth confirming this array is actually populated during the merge step.

findings.title: Harvest `claude -p` call has no file-scope restriction and only the failure-patterns.md diff is committed
findings.desc: Unlike the per-task implement prompt (which enforces an explicit FILE SCOPE CONSTRAINT), the post-merge harvest prompt only tells the model to "append... to docs/thoughts/failure-patterns.md" with no restriction against touching other files. The script then checks/stages/commits only `$FP_LIB`'s diff (`git diff --quiet -- "$FP_LIB"`), so if the model edits or creates any other file, that change is left dirty and uncommitted in the shared main worktree, silently bleeding into subsequent rounds instead of failing loudly or being discarded.

findings.title: Failure-pattern harvest silently no-ops if `claude` fails or produces malformed output
findings.desc: The `claude -p ... 2>/dev/null || true` swallows all stderr/errors, and there is no post-check that the appended entries conform to the schema (unlike the code-review gate's `parse_code_review_red`/`code_review_gate_verdict` fail-closed helpers). A malformed or partial append (or an outright failed run) would go unnoticed, silently degrading the failure-pattern library the ADR calls "cross-round learning."

findings.title: Tier C ("full parity") is instruction-only, with no gate verifying compliance
findings.desc: The ADR's Consequences claim the loop "now produces the same artifact trail as a human PR ... so a round is auditable the way a PR is," but nothing in the validation gates (including the new gate 1h, already committed) checks that a task actually ran `/verify`, executed the review-fix loop, or wrote a retro doc — a task can skip all of Tier C and still pass every mechanical/code-review gate and merge. The claimed parity is aspirational/prompt-only, not enforced.

findings.title: grep pipeline crash on empty file
findings.desc: If `docs/thoughts/failure-patterns.md` exists but contains no `FP-[0-9]+` entries yet, `grep` will exit 1. Under `set -eo pipefail`, this command substitution failure will crash the script immediately after tasks are merged, preventing the round summary from executing. Append `|| true` to the pipeline to safely fall back to 0.

findings.title: `git diff --quiet` ignores staged changes and `git commit` lacks path specifier
findings.desc: If the autonomous agent stages `$FP_LIB` (`git add`), `git diff --quiet` (which checks unstaged changes only) returns 0 and skips the commit. Additionally, `git commit -m` without a path specifier will accidentally commit any other currently staged files in the index. Use `! git diff --quiet HEAD -- "$FP_LIB"` and `git commit -m "..." -- "$FP_LIB"`.
